management_remarks.speaker: Moderator
management_remarks.text: Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to the Q2 and H1 FY27 Earnings Conference Call hosted by Tamilnad Mercantile Bank Limited. This conference call may contain forward-looking statements about the company, which are based on the beliefs, opinions and expectation of the company as on date of this call. These statements are not the guarantee of future performance and involve risks and uncertainties that are difficult to predict. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode, and there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need assistance during the conference call, please signal an operator by pressing star then zero on your touchtone phone. Please note that this conference is being recorded. On the call today, we have the following management representatives: Mr. Salee S. Nair, Managing Director; Mr. Sanjoy Kumar Goel, Chief Financial Officer. I now hand the conference over to Mr. Salee S. Nair, Managing Director from Tamilnad Mercantile Bank Limited. Thank you, and over to you, sir.

management_remarks.speaker: Salee S. Nair
management_remarks.text: Thank you. Thank you very much, and thanks for attending this con call from Tamilnad Mercantile Bank. And I'm sure most of you would have already seen our results on the website and on the exchanges. The quarterly performance has been as anticipated. We have been maintaining the trend of growth that we delivered last quarter. We have actually exceeded that, and this is something that we have been doing it quarter after quarter for the past 7 quarters. I think it's the 8th quarter where we have exceeded our previous performance. And to delve into some of these highlights, very clearly, the growth has accelerated and the profit is at record level. And when we look at the business growth itself, the total business grew 27.25% year-on-year, which is almost 3x our own 10-year CAGR of 9.41%. So, this CAGR is also moving up on the basis of the rising growth. And this growth is highest year-on-year growth in the last 18 years. So, that's something that we are fairly proud of. And it's also 8% faster than the industry. So, the delta today in terms of growth is 8% over the industry's growth that TMB has delivered. And this growth has driven a strong net profit, the highest ever, INR451 crores highest ever net profit. And that net profit has come out of the core business growth. These are not on account of exceptional results, largely driven by the core business, by a very strong net interest income. Apart from that, let me also say that the strength that we are adding to the balance sheet in terms of other measures, one of them we have taken based, looking forward into the ECL norms that will come on the 1st of April 2027. We have, in anticipation, provided fully for SMA 1 and SMA 2 as per ECL norms. If that's something that we have done this quarter, if you recall, in quarter 1 of the current year, FY27, we had also provided fully for the stressed non-fund facilities. So, that was last quarter, this quarter, SMA 1 and SMA 2, we have fully provided as per ECL norms. Tamilnad Mercantile Bank Limited October 26, 2026 And of course, NPA, the gross and net, continues to decline. The net NPA is at 0.14%. The capital adequacy is at 32.39%. The balance sheet has also moved up quite sharply by 24.49% year-on-year. And this has resulted in the overall growth and the profit has resulted in an ROE of 16.92%, quarterly earnings per share is at INR28.49 and the shareholders' fund is today 12.53% of the balance sheet. Just to give you a little more color on the numbers itself, the total business stands at INR1,30,237 crores is up 27.25% and contributed by deposits growing at 25.49%, which stands today at INR69,546 crores and advances up 29.32%, standing at INR60,691 crores. CASA grew about 16.26%, RAM at 28.96%, and on the earnings side, as I said that the profit has been delivered on a strong net interest income, the net interest income for the quarter stands at INR807 crores, up INR35.17 crores. The operating profit after expenses is INR642 crores, up 41.80%. As I said earlier, the net profit is record, the highest ever this bank has clocked at INR451 crores, up 42.09% year-on-year. And ROA, the return on assets, stands at 2.18%. ROE, 16.92%. So, that's where we stand. Of course, when you look at the cost to income, it is 38.28%. That's where it stands as on 30th of September. The unsecured exposure is bare 20 basis points. Our RAM focus continues. It stands at 94.33%. The net interest margin is year-on-year up 36 basis, stands at 4.19%. Sequentially, it stands at we have lost 10 basis. It was 4.29% for and I did explain why it was 4.29% last quarter in the last con call. Profit per employee stands at almost INR35 lakhs, and that is up 36.45%. Gross NPA 0.61% and net NPA is 0.14%. The credit cost is at 9 basis points, 0.09%, and the slippage is again 6 basis points. But this year, on book PCR is 77.49% and the overall PCR is at 96.61%. SMA 0, 1, 2, I repeat, it is 0 included SMA 0, 1, 2 is at 1.67%, which is that if you look at your NPA 0.61% and SMA of 1.67%, your portfolio at risk one day today, 30th of September, was at 2.28%. As I said earlier, the stressed NFB, we have provided 100% and SMA 1 and 2, we have also provided 100% as per the ECL norms. So, just to run through some of the numbers. CASA 16.26% is the growth. Term deposit, the total deposit growth of 25.49% has been driven by the term deposits, which stands at almost 29%. And if you look at the number itself, I think the non-callable deposits' share in the incremental term deposits, incremented term deposit for the half year stands at INR7,570 crores, 40.62% of that came in the form of noncallable deposits. As you're aware, noncallable deposits are deposits which cannot be paid before the maturity. So, there's no prepayment of that. So, from that perspective, the deposit mix resource security that much more stronger. FCNR (B), we did about USD51.94 million, not something that we can write home about. So overall, the FCNR (B)deposit growth has been 47.14%. So, it should not be one of the better Tamilnad Mercantile Bank Limited October 26, 2026 stories that we want to put on the table is just about USD51.94 million. And the advances 29.32%, riding on the RAM. If you look at the MSME, as I promised, has inched up and today stands at 23.62%. We also had; I think there's a lot of talk going on the gold loan portfolio. The gold loan portfolio, we have put out our sensitivity on it at 20% or 3.1% of our gold loan will be above the market. It is just a 3.13%. The portfolio LTV stands at 62.35%. The overall, the portfolio is at about 48%, almost stable. It was about 47% something earlier. It's about 48% now. Unsecured exposure remains minimal at 20 basis points. So, when I get into some of the ratios, I'll just take you through some of the ratios. Fresh slippage, I just mentioned 6 basis. Before I come to the ratio, let me also give you some color on the expected credit loss. We have done a calculation of the impact as of 30th of September '26, that comes to about INR384 crores. The new norms and expected credit loss would be INR385 crores. And I think if you check into the Slide 29, we have given a color of how we intend to tackle it. We are already, our provisions done this quarter, last quarter and the existing contingency provision together today covers almost 80% of that at INR304.24 crores. So, on the ratios, cost of deposits has moved up. Yes, one of the reasons is that it is moving our share of term deposits as you can see, the CASA went up only 15.26%, where our term deposits actually grew close to 29%. So, it is having an impact on the cost of deposit, that's 5.85%. This was anticipated and we have tweaked our advances portfolio to cover for this increase because focus has been more on the resource security for our growth and we are anticipating that we did tweak the advances and that also shows up in yield advances, which has moved up to 10.32% from the 10.10% earlier. Cost of funds is at 5.93%. We have picked up almost INR1,000 crores of refinance during the quarter at 7.5%. It's also pushing up the cost of funds. And consequently, the NIM sequentially has come down about 10 basis. But it's still on a year-on-year basis, it's still significantly 36 basis up. And credit costs, like I said, is just 9 basis points. Our calculations show that the expected credit loss for the bank is INR385 crores. And like I said, in the last quarter, we did provide fully 100% for the non-fund facilities, which are under stress. This quarter, we have provided 100% for SMA 1 and 2 as per ECL norms. So, but the total upfront provision that we have done for the ECL is INR54.24 crores along with the existing contingency provision available of INR250 crores. We have a provision available of INR304.24 crores against the INR385 crores that is required to cover the expected credit loss. That's almost a provision of almost 80%. I was also telling about the cost of deposits. It has moved up from 5.68% to 5.85%, that is anticipated. When you look at your term deposit moving up almost 29%, and the CASA moving up at a slower pace, 16.26%. The cost of deposits was anticipated to go up. We did, like I said, anticipate and we tweaked our advances portfolio to guard against that and that is also having an impact on the advances portfolio where it has moved up from 10.10% to 10.32%. Tamilnad Mercantile Bank Limited October 26, 2026 Cost of funds is at 5.93%, we did pick up some refinance in the quarter from SIDBI about 7% to 7.5%, that's slightly pushed it up. The NIM consequently is at 4.19%. It is up 36 basis from on a year-on-year basis. But sequentially, as the term deposit portfolio is improving, it has actually gone down about 10 basis points. Also, the credit cost is at 9 basis. Capital adequacy at 32.39% basis and cost-to-income ratio, like I said, has consistently been moving down, trending down and stands at 38.28%. PCR at 77.49%, that is the on book PCR. I can also tell you that now our leverage and NSFR, LCR, etcetera are on a good footing. Our leverage ratio against what is required to be done at 3.50%, our leverage ratio stands at 11.99% and LCR is at 139.43% and NSFR is at 146.15%. We have also given you some color on where how the CD ratio can move forward to what extent we have cushion left and that's also there in the presentation, if you refer, Page number 33, the CD ratio that is possible for us given the fact that our net-worth today at 12.53% contribution to the balance sheet, we can go up to a CD ratio of 98%. And today, the CD ratio stands at just 87.27%, which is better than what we did last quarter. The profit per employee, it has gone up 35% to INR35 crores. Business per employee stands at sorry, the profit per employee goes up to INR35 lakhs, sorry. It is not crores, it is lakhs. But business per employee is at INR25 crores. We did open our 9 branches in the half year and we are committed to open 60 and the process is on for the other branches to be opened. Year-on-year, we did open about 37 branches and 15 of these branches were opened outside the state of Tamil Nadu. And when we end the year 60 branches, we hope to open 20-plus branches outside the state of Tamil Nadu. So, I think we have also given you some color of the kind of structural changes we are making in the presentation. I think you can go through that. And there are questions we are here to answer that. So over to you, guys. Thank you.
